mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a 0.25% increase in FEDFUNDS, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of instances following a 0.3pp rise in UNRATE, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances following a 1% increase in RSAFS, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a weakening supply side, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following a 0.5% decline in INDPRO, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.5% and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances following the specified joint movement in PAYEMS and UNRATE, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL) coupled with a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances under the specified conditions for CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong demand in the housing market, which boosts related sectors and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances following a sustained increase in HOUST, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in GDP (GDPC1) signals a weakening economy, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following a 1% decline in GDPC1, this hypothesis is rejected.
